_comment: Reproducibility gate policy for scripts/repro_gate.py. Declares this corpus's adapter and its reproducibility ratchet. See repro_gate.py for the verdict vocabulary.
_criterion_note: The 'space' adapter measures >= threshold contiguous token overlap against a fresh extraction, not byte equality, because each text.txt is the official text re-cut and re-wrapped (see extract.py). The stored bytes are separately hash-pinned. Until every record is converted (below), 'reproduced' here is a weaker claim than in the other four corpora, honestly recorded per record as overlap_pct.
_byte_equality_migration: 2026-07-22: scripts/derive_text.py reproduces a record BYTE-EXACTLY as extract -> slice -> reflow -> mechanical rules -> recorded corrections, with each stage declared in corrections/<corpus_id>/<version_id>.json. This exists because the gap was NOT sloppiness: the stored texts are more faithful than the raw extraction (a human rejoined line-break hyphenation, stripped markdown emphasis, repaired a broken private-use glyph, and restored a signatory name absent from the PDF text layer). Those repairs are correct and must be kept — but while they lived only in the stored bytes, nothing recorded that a human had changed anything, or why. CONVERTED SO FAR: 1 of 23 (nat/usa/space-resources-2015, the simplest record, used to prove the pipeline). The two criteria coexist deliberately: repro_gate.py keeps the overlap criterion so nothing regresses, while derive_text.py is the stricter parallel gate that grows as records are converted. Switch the adapter to byte equality only when all 23 carry a corrections file.
